The only open copy is the Rosetta Project 11-page phonology excerpt; the remaining chapters (ch. 2 on canonical patterns / vowel neutralization onward) are not open (HathiTrust is search-only and the catalog probe hit an automated-access block, so nothing further could be read). sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Eastern Sara Languages, 8th ed. Cuenca: Morkeg Books (Sara Language Project; NEH-funded). General 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' + 'Introduction to Eastern Sara' (Mbay data cited passim; Mbay lexicon deliberately omitted, cf. Keegan 2009).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Tone section: 'All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low'; HL on final syllable of polysyllabic loans becomes Mid in sentences; vowel-neutralisation (barred-i) patterns in CVCV morphemes. No accent/stress statement anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: only 'unaccented e' as an English pronunciation gloss).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 1997. A Reference Grammar of Mbay (LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 14). München: Lincom Europa. Chapter 1 'Segmental phonology' incl. 1.4 'Tonal system', printed pp. 1-11 (Rosetta Project excerpt 'Mbay Phonology', archive.org rosettaproject_myb_phon-1).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent. Describes 7 vowels, 17 consonants, vowel length contrast, and (p.10-11) 'three level tones in Mbay: low, mid, and high', TBUs = vowels, syllable-final sonorants, syllabic nasals; restricted HL and ML sequences. Only use of the word 'stress' (p.10) concerns the position of stress in Arabic source words of loans (V́mV > mb). Chapter 2 ff. (morpheme structure, vowel neutralisation 2.2.3) not in the excerpt.
